newsitem.title: USA: Continental Cable pleased with valuation.
newsitem.headline: Continental Cable pleased with valuation.

text.p: Continental Cablevision Inc Chief Executive Officer Amos Hostetter said on Monday he believed the cable television company would receive "fair value" in its deal with U S West Inc's U S West Media Group.
Earlier Monday, the companies announced that U S West Media stock would be valued at $21 for the purpose of their previously-announced merger.
That is several dollars more than the level at which the shares have been trading recently and just above the lower limit of the collar set previously.

"It was not a controversial vote," Hostetter told reporters during a conference call. Hostetter said in the earlier statement that Continental thought U S West Media stock was currently undervalued by the stock market.
The stock was trading up 5/8 at 17-1/2 in midafternoon.
A U S West Media spokesman denied a Wall Street Journal report that said the company was mulling adding additional cash to the deal.

Under the previously announced deal worth $5.3 billion, some $1 billion is in U S West Inc preferred stock, $1 billion to $1.5 billion is in cash and $2.8 billion to $3.3 billion is in U S West Media stock. Spokesman Steve Lang said those elements have not been revised.

The deal also has U S West assuming some $6.5 billion in Continental's debt, up from $5.5 billion when the deal was announced. Executives said the increased debt can be attributed to Continental upgrading its system and had been factored into the deal.
The original deal called for the value of U S West Media stock to be valued at between 15 percent above or below $24.50.
Chuck Lillis, U S West Media's chief executive, said the company was convinced that the use of hybrid fiber/coaxial cable technology, or HFC, represented the greatest competitive advantage.
Hostetter said Continental had upgraded about 25 percent of its system to HFC and planned to complete the process by the end of 1998.
